title: OA CREATING A STYLE - the style-construction doctrine: the three forms, the principal method choice, the Table 69 mechanics, the weapons roll and the Special Maneuvers intro
audit_label: R690 OA creating a style audit
audit_comment: OA round seventy-seven (capture pp. 225-227): the Creating a Style doctrine - the three forms with the principal method, the Table 69 mechanics, the weapons roll and the Special Maneuvers intro, single-pass pins per the Chapter 9 provenance shift

banner.title: OA CREATING A STYLE, printed capture pp. 225-227 - the style-construction round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture - the sole surviving pass per the R679 provenance shift. THE FRAME: the DM encouraged to create new styles taught by NPC masters, the general characteristics chosen then the values, terms and abilities selected from the lists. THE THREE FORMS: hard - muscles and bones, direct, offensive; soft - the inner power, fluid and circular, defensive, the attacker's force against him, attacking only after the commitment; combined - the best of each, physical balanced with psychic; all using the unusual weapons. THE PRINCIPAL METHOD: the most common fighting method, every style incorporating moves from other methods - the single form the certain defeat. THE MECHANICS: one form and one method per style; the mods totaled - the AC from the 10, the attacks style-specific, the damage rounded up to the die (6 the d6, 4 the d4, 5 the d6), the body part free; the 1d4-minus-two weapons of the martial-arts-only list. THE MANEUVERS: the intensive study, the combat cost (one or more attacks) and the movement cost (no attacks), the method organization with the hard/soft identity and the crossover; the 1d8 roll of the principal method or the Mental and Physical Training, the 1-3 roll of the other methods - the arsenal of tactics; the ranking progression from 1 up, the higher learned only beneath; the gradual learning; the Mental and Physical Training learnable in any style. The prose codifies per the R431 calculus

consts.name: djdOACreateACBase
consts.comment: the style armor class base - the AC Mod. of the form and the method totaled, the number subtracted from 10 to get the armor class of the style (print capture p. 226)

consts.name: djdOACreateWeaponsDie
consts.comment: the weapons-taught die - the DM rolls 1d4 and subtracts two from the result, the number of weapons taught under the style (print capture p. 226)

consts.name: djdOACreateWeaponsShift
consts.comment: the weapons-taught shift - the two subtracted from the 1d4 roll (print capture p. 226)

consts.name: djdOACreateManeuverFirstDie
consts.comment: the first maneuver roll - roll 1d8, the number of special maneuvers chosen from the principal method of the style or from the Mental and Physical Training lists (print capture p. 227)

consts.name: djdOACreateManeuverSecondDie
consts.comment: the second maneuver roll - a roll of 1-3 made to find the number of maneuvers chosen from other methods (or again the Mental and Physical Training category) (print capture p. 227)

bools.name: djdOACreateDoctrine
bools.comment: the creation frame - in addition to the common styles the DM is encouraged to create new styles taught by various NPC masters, a style created by choosing the general characteristics then selecting values, terms and abilities from the lists given in the text (print capture p. 225)

bools.name: djdOACreateHardForm
bools.comment: the hard form - emphasizing the use of the muscles and bones for power, very direct movements, generally offensive, stressing the attack (print capture p. 225)

bools.name: djdOACreateSoftForm
bools.comment: the soft form - relying more on the inner power of the character, the movements fluid and circular, generally more defensive, diverting the attacker with his own force against him and attacking only after the enemy has committed himself, the training more mentally oriented (print capture p. 225)

bools.name: djdOACreateCombinedForm
bools.comment: the combined form - using the best practices from each, the circular and gentle defensive movements combined with swift and direct attacks, the physical training balanced with the psychic (print capture p. 225)

bools.name: djdOACreateUnusualWeapons
bools.comment: the weapons clause - all styles can make use of a number of unusual weapons (print capture p. 225)

bools.name: djdOACreatePrincipalMethod
bools.comment: the principal method choice - the fighting method most commonly used in the style, the character more often than not using it when attacking, each method describing the most common means of attack (print capture p. 225)

bools.name: djdOACreateOtherMethods
bools.comment: the other-methods rule - every style incorporates moves from other methods, since reliance on a single form would certainly mean defeat (print capture p. 225)

bools.name: djdOACreateOneFormOneMethod
bools.comment: the selection rule - the DM must select one form and one principal method for each style (print capture p. 226)

bools.name: djdOACreateAttacksStyleSpecific
bools.comment: the attacks rule - the #AT Mod. of the form and the method totaled is the number of attacks allowed in a melee round when fighting in this style, applying to no other style nor when fighting with normal weapons (print capture p. 226)

bools.name: djdOACreateDamageRounding
bools.comment: the damage rule - the Damage Mod. of the form and the method totaled, rounded up to the nearest die size used in the game: a total of 6 the 1d6, of 4 the 1d4, of 5 the 1d6 - the basic damage done when fighting in the style (print capture p. 226)

bools.name: djdOACreateBodyPartFree
bools.comment: the body part rule - the listed part or parts most commonly used, kicking the feet, throwing the whole body; so long as the body part is unbound or free to move the character can still attack effectively with the style (print capture p. 226)

bools.name: djdOACreateWeaponsList
bools.comment: the weapons selection - the weapons selected from those that can be used in martial arts only (print capture p. 226)

bools.name: djdOACreateManeuversLast
bools.comment: the creation order - finally the DM must determine the special maneuvers used by the style (print capture p. 226)

bools.name: djdOAManeuversIntensiveStudy
bools.comment: the maneuvers frame - actions and abilities requiring intensive study and skill to learn, giving the user greater-than-normal results; some attempted during a fight (Flying Kick, One Finger), others constant abilities always in effect (Ironskin, Blind Fighting) (print capture pp. 226-227)

bools.name: djdOAManeuversCombatCost
bools.comment: the combat maneuver cost - combat maneuvers risky, failure often leaving the character in an exposed or dangerous position, the maneuver costing one or more of his attacks for the melee round (print capture p. 227)

bools.name: djdOAManeuversMovementCost
bools.comment: the movement maneuver cost - a movement maneuver counts as movement, preventing the character from making any attacks that round unless the maneuver notes otherwise (print capture p. 227)

bools.name: djdOAManeuversMethodOrganized
bools.comment: the organization - all maneuvers organized according to the principal method of fighting used, kicking covering kicks, movement the leaps, tumbles, dives and acrobatics; each maneuver identified as hard, soft or hard/soft, matching the general classification of the style, the crossover not prevented (print capture p. 227)

bools.name: djdOAManeuversSecondRollOthers
bools.comment: the second-roll scope - the 1-3 roll finding the maneuvers chosen from other methods, all styles usually incorporating a few maneuvers from other methods to provide the character an arsenal of tactics (print capture p. 227)

bools.name: djdOAManeuversRanking
bools.comment: the ranking rule - the maneuvers ranked by difficulty, the lower the number the easier to learn and execute; when selecting there must be a progression from 1 on up, not within a single method, more than one at the same level allowed - a style beginning Circle Kick (1), Flying Kick (2), All-Around Sight (2), ending Backward Kick (3); a higher difficulty maneuver learned only if those beneath it are already learned (print capture p. 227)

bools.name: djdOAManeuversGradualLearning
bools.comment: the gradual rule - special maneuvers not gained immediately upon learning the style, requiring extra training and learned gradually (print capture p. 227)

bools.name: djdOAMentalPhysicalAnyStyle
bools.comment: the Mental and Physical Training category - maneuvers learnable in any style because of the methods of practice and discipline of the training (print capture p. 227)
